newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian stocks eke out record close.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian stocks eke out record close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2594 +7 US 30yr cl 7.03 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.365 -0.090 Gold NY 344.70 Lon fix 343.65
*Stocks lock in modest gains on way to record high and record close, mixed trade. Volume 370.35 million, value A$763.27 million, 1,136 stocks traded, 346 steady, 464 up, 326 down.
The Australian share market kept a firm grip on early gains to close firmer on Wednesday, capturing record highs along the way.
The All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points up at 2,585.2, having touched a record high of 2,590.4, surpassing the previous mark of 2,585.8 set on Tuesday.
June share price index futures were seven points higher at 2,594, an 8.2 point premium to the index.
Despite the milestones reached, it was a day of modest gains in middling trade with gains by some of the big banks and key industrials outweighing light losses among most of the leaders.
Brokers said the dividend had surprised on the upside and the price had been adjusted accordingly.
Sector leader National Australia Bank did not fare so well, losing 1.5 percent to A$18.66 as traders saw more attractive opportunities elsewhere in the sector.
"I think you have seen some switching and CommBank and ANZ have been the winners there. The rest have been a bit lacklustre," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Conglomerate Lend Lease ended up 20 cents at A$25.40 after it said its ISSC Australia joint venture with Telstra Corp AOT.AX and IBM had been finalised.

Market leader BHP bounced off support at the A$18.20 level to end steady at A$18.39. From Monday's high of A$19.42 prior to the fourth quarter profit warning, the bellwether had lost over six percent of its value.
Elsewhere, the interest rate sensitive building materials stocks impressed before fading late in the day.
The pick of the bunch expected to get a boost from last Friday's rate cut was Boral Ltd, which added seven cents or 1.8 percent to A$4.04.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was active ahead of Thursday's May series expiry with 56,740 traded. Futures trade was moderate with 6,342 contracts traded.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields closed higher, primarily in response to weakness in U.S. Treasuries, although the short end outperformed once again and was still benefitting from last week's rate cut. By 5.00 p.m (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.63 percent, up 7.56 Tuesday.
The Australian dollar tracked sideways for most of the day but the routine performance belied a backstage struggle as offshore sellers vied to break support.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the local currency had edged higher to US$0.7659/64 from US$0.7650/55 here late Tuesday.
